purpose: Independent behavioral confirmation of the complete V2-M1 through V2-M3 authorization chain on fresh data

amendment_record.reason: An oracle-association diagnostic (ground-truth blob-to-track matching substituted for the beam search, everything else in OnlineEntityGraph/IntegratedSelfWorldAgent left untouched) established that V2-I1's identity_consistency gate failure (0.219 vs the 0.90 gate) is caused entirely by association quality in `_probabilistic_assign`, not by track-state corruption (V6, a null result) or by the integration layer's own pruning (a separate oracle run showed 0 evictions across 3200 steps once association was correct) - a perfect-association oracle reaches identity_consistency=0.9691. A four-expert review (multi-object-tracking, estimation-theory, this project's own protocol discipline, and an adversarial red-team pass) of a proposed fix converged on rejecting a temporal-hysteresis/stickiness design (risks entrenching a mis-association rather than only preventing new ones, and adds new per-track state whose interaction with _propagate_membership/_edges/pruning would need the same scrutiny that caught a real bug in V6) in favor of a stateless, uncertainty-adaptive gating design: `_probabilistic_assign`'s motion_cost currently normalizes every track's prediction error against the same fixed 0.32 scale regardless of that track's own RLS confidence, which cannot distinguish a well-established, confidently-tracked entity from a track that was only just created - exactly the condition present when a confident track loses a close encounter to a rival under the current flat scale. This amendment adds a `confidence_adaptive_gating_weight` constructor parameter (default 0.0, a hard no-op: `_motion_cost_scale` returns exactly 0.32, the value every existing caller has always used, without evaluating any covariance-dependent expression). When enabled, the per-track motion_cost scale becomes `0.32 * exp(weight * (6.0 - action @ track.covariance @ action))`, where `action @ track.covariance @ action` is the RLS's own already-computed prediction-variance term (previously computed inline during the theta update but never used for candidate scoring) and 6.0 is the reference variance a brand-new track's own initial covariance produces for a unit action, so a fresh track behaves identically to the disabled case. The originally-hypothesized direction (tighten confident tracks, on the reasoning that a confidently-tracked entity is the one that loses close encounters to rivals under a flat scale) was tested first via a pre-registered calibration-set sweep and measured WORSE than baseline at every tested weight; a sign-flipped version (widen confident tracks, tighten uncertain ones) measured better at every tested weight, peaking around weight~=0.2. The likely mechanism, revised after this empirical correction: a still-uncertain track (freshly created or long unmatched) is the one most at risk of being prematurely fragmented by ordinary detection jitter read as a miss, not the already-stable ones; loosening its tolerance lets it survive to become well-established. The shipped formula uses this corrected (empirically-verified, not first-guessed) direction. This design introduces no new per-track state, only reads an existing field, so it cannot interact with _propagate_membership/_edges/pruning the way V6's state-mutating reset could. A pre-registered, time-boxed sweep of the four already-exposed association parameters (identity_switch_penalty_weight, association_commitment, match_radius, association_miss_cost) was run first on a held-out calibration subset of the V2-I1 development seeds and did not clear its own pre-registered go/no-go threshold (validation-set identity_consistency >= 0.35; best result was 0.244), so those parameter values were discarded rather than adopted, and this mechanism-level amendment was made regardless of that outcome, per the pre-registered plan. Verified empirically, not just argued: development-split results for V2-M2 (all three association modes, plus the legacy path) and V2-M3 (plus its no-causal-likelihood ablation) were captured before this change and re-run after it with the new code's default parameter; every field is byte-for-byte identical except cpu_wall_seconds (a timing measurement, not a behavioral output). No existing caller (v2_m2.py, v2_m3_hypotheses.py, v2_m1_m3_confirmation.py) passes the new parameter, so none of their behavior changes. The already-published v2 confirmation result and its reported metrics remain the authoritative one-shot evidence for the historical M1-M3 chain; this amendment does not authorize or require a new confirmation run.

scope_statement.claim: Fresh-data behavioral confirmation of control discovery, probabilistic identity retention, and calibrated complete-body graph selection
not_claimed: Direct serialization or state handoff from the historical M1 implementation into M2
More than two complete body hypotheses
scope_statement.composition_fact: M2 relearns control relations and M3 extends the M2 entity graph; the historical M1 agent is a stage-specific mechanism check, not a serialized upstream state provider

decision_rule: Authorize design of unprivileged V2-M4 only if every fixed gate passes on the one-shot fresh confirmation. Development results cannot authorize progression, and confirmation failure cannot be repaired by changing this protocol or rerunning its confirmation seeds.
